title: Smart Choices: How Many Small Savings Schemes Do You Need?
description: Holding multiple small savings schemes like PPF, NSC, KVP, and SSY simultaneously is often unnecessary and can complicate your portfolio. Each scheme serves a.

faq.q: Can NRIs invest in all small savings schemes?
faq.a: No. Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) can continue to operate existing PPF accounts until maturity but cannot open new ones. NRIs are generally not eligible to invest in NSC, KVP, or SSY schemes.

faq.q: Are the interest rates for these schemes fixed for the entire tenure?
faq.a: No, the interest rates for PPF, NSC, KVP, and SSY are reviewed and declared quarterly by the Ministry of Finance. Once invested, the rate for NSC and KVP is fixed for the entire tenure, but for PPF and SSY, the interest rate applicable changes annually based on the prevailing rates.

faq.q: What is the maximum investment limit for these schemes?
faq.a: For PPF and SSY, the maximum annual investment is ₹1.5 lakhs. For NSC, there is no upper limit for investment, but only up to ₹1.5 lakhs qualifies for Section 80C deduction. For KVP, there is no upper investment limit.

faq.q: Can I open multiple accounts for the same scheme?
faq.a: Generally, no. An individual can open only one PPF account. For SSY, an account can be opened for a maximum of two girl children in a family (or three in case of the first birth resulting in twins or the second birth resulting in twins). For NSC and KVP, multiple certificates can be purchased, but they are typically held in the name of a single individual or jointly.

faq.q: Are these schemes better than bank Fixed Deposits (FDs)?
faq.a: Often, yes, especially due to tax benefits. PPF and SSY offer EEE tax status, which is superior to bank FDs where interest is fully taxable (though TDS may not apply below certain limits). NSC offers 80C benefits on principal. While bank FDs offer more liquidity, small savings schemes often provide better post-tax returns and government backing, making them a safe and attractive option for specific goals.

faq.q: Can I use these schemes as collateral for loans?
faq.a: Yes, PPF accounts can be pledged as collateral for loans from the 3rd to 6th financial year. NSC certificates can also be pledged or transferred as security to banks or financial institutions. KVP certificates can be transferred to an authorised bank or Post Office. SSY accounts generally cannot be used as collateral.

faq.q: What happens if I miss a minimum contribution in PPF or SSY?
faq.a: If you miss the minimum annual contribution (₹500 for PPF, ₹250 for SSY), your account becomes dormant. It can be revived by paying a penalty along with the minimum due amount for each year of default.
